decisions.summary: One margin seated once; the ladder only past a margin seating no house; partial seating refused; rescue, withheld re-seat, early stop, 12:1 refusal removed
decisions.why: FR-001, FR-004-FR-006; unchanged since the CLEAR review.

decisions.summary: Growth widens past GROW_LEVELS with no radius test; still says 'AMENDED with D4 (research R1): the table is one level, every direction and ring of the old three offered at once'
decisions.why: The one-level table is the decision D4 WITHDRAWS. FR-003a: the growth's breadth MUST be main's; the GM (Amendment 3): 'the tie-break thing for the real speedup' - the one-level table was the +11.9% slowdown. The widening past the table (FR-002) is within; the stale sentence contradicts the request and D4.

decisions.summary: FIELD_REACH_FT and within_field_reach deleted; seat window, free-ground box and free_seats box the canvas; ways/law.py constant untouched
decisions.why: FR-003 as written. Note: the engine as landed builds the seat region and free-ground grid over boundary.seating_window (twice the households' seating radius, clipped to the canvas), not the canvas - D3's text is no longer what is built (see D10).

decisions.summary: Main's GROW_LEVELS (8/12/16); heap keyed by 20 ft TIE_RING_FT ring of distance from the margin's seat center, field distance breaking ties within a ring, then exact distance, then insertion order; the 16x3 level withdrawn
decisions.why: FR-003a and SC-002a verbatim; the GM: 'all else being equal, try this first' and 'the tie-break thing for the real speedup'. Verified main's key is distance from the margin's seat center (origin/main growth.py) and the ring cannot outrank it.

decisions.summary: recheck_passages keeps only its in-place ending; relay removed; now runs after the gap pass
decisions.why: FR-001 and FR-013's last sentence (the end-in-place check against the tree the ways make).

decisions.summary: 0029/0032/0081 drawing pages; claims citing the reach removed
Occasions: placement-changed farmhouse on the nucleated pool maps; village lane for the ways laid in the gaps
grow_gap = MIN_WEB_GAP (18 ft) + the 2 ft parting = 20 ft; a tight seat parted at TIGHT_GAP_PX from its one neighbor only
decisions.why: FR-011: 'at least' the threading gap, the exemption pairwise. Constants verified (consts.MIN_WEB_GAP = 2 x 7 + 4 = 18; main's gap 16). The GM: 'a slightly higher minimum distance from your neighbors'.

decisions.summary: Lane-ground raster in SeatRegion; one predicate opens() admits an ordinary seat and refuses a tight one; flooded also from the window's edge 'as today'
decisions.why: The window-edge seeding (and region.offer passing a seat past the window unjudged) admits a seat whose lane ground is not shown connected to the way out (FR-012). Today that over-count is 'settled by the placer's own corridor search' (region.py) - which D11 removes. It is legitimate only because, with every two homesteads a threading gap apart, the pockets it can miss are those against the paddy, water or map edge, which the GM accepted outright: 'I'm not concerned about the other lane-blocking map features because ... it's okay for people to cut through neighbors' yards in a pinch'. The plan must say so rather than 'as today'.

decisions.summary: No per-seat corridor search, judgment or reservation for an ordinary household; exit strip and field corridor kept; a passage household's walk still barred
decisions.why: The walk bar is a path reserved per household before the last stands (SC-008's literal 'reserved'). Legitimate: it is not a search (the GM: 'drop the search entirely'), and without it a later house may stand on the walk of the tight seat that FR-011 and FR-013 keep. The access tree exists only on the nucleated form (stages.py), so no other form keeps a per-seat search.

decisions.summary: gap_ways.py at the seating's end: raster, flood from the way out costed to the gap's middle, per-house local way out (6 exits), traced with a T-join within 25 ft, taut, admitted by the corridor's own predicate, reserved and recorded
decisions.why: FR-014 clause by clause: dooryard, gaps' middle, way out or an earlier way at a T, today's lane law, laid before the other parts and kept clear. The GM: 'I still want A for how it shapes the map'.

decisions.summary: A household the gap pass does not reach recorded reached across the nearest household with a laid way (kind pinch), the 3 ft adjoining condition not binding, counted in meta.pinch_passages
decisions.why: FR-014's fallback; the GM: 'it's okay for people to cut through neighbors' yards in a pinch' states no adjoining condition. 'No lawful way reaches' is decided by the pass's bounded search, the same standard every corridor in the engine has; counted, so a miss is visible.

decisions.summary: 0081 and 0029 drawing pages (gap, no search while seated, ways in the gaps as a GUESS, the pinch; nearer the field all else equal); claims re-checked by impl-drift
decisions.why: FR-008, US3 scenarios 3-4. 0029 currently states the withdrawn 'every direction at once' rule in its comment and is the page D14 rewrites.
